title: Legacy Python chat import retains text but discards source tree, unknown fields and attachment linkage

evidence.actual: Five source nodes (including system/tool) become three user/assistant message records. Parents, original IDs, model metadata, unknown message/conversation fields and attachment linkage are not retained in the imported records or explicit graph links. Original selected source file itself is not modified.
evidence.no_overclaim: No claim about native archive import; no claim that original source bytes are physically deleted.

actual_impact: The Python GUI/headless entrypoint cannot supply the requested lossless conversation/relationship projection from its persisted output. ZIP temporary extraction does not add a versioned source selector or reference.

title: HTML fallback orders turns by role pattern rather than source sequence

actual_impact: Headless and GUI callers of the same parser receive a changed conversation sequence; temporal/context relations cannot be trusted from this projection.

title: Frozen project source bytes and headless typed renderer are real reusable mechanisms

evidence.actual: Real typed dataset -> WorkbenchRepository/ObjectStore -> ResearchProjectsService pins hash-checked copies. Source approval change reports CHANGED; simulated owner loss reports UNAVAILABLE; historical archive bytes remain equal. Missing original live blob gives actual read error while frozen export remains available. Native file-backed DB reopen preserves history. SSR calls shared FigureCanvas; exact raw CSV including unmapped column survives research ZIP.
evidence.important_boundary: Project statuses inspect metadata/snapshot, not byte fetch availability. Missing original blob is a separate read failure; a CURRENT/CHANGED status is not evidence of a successful live fetch.

actual_impact: These existing mechanisms can support a composed resource path. They do not implement generic ZIP graph traversal, independent resource-policy axes or a browser roundtrip.
